answer: One concrete defense: new agents earn voting weight only after an existing agent vouches for them by bonding its own stake. If the newcomer is later caught colluding, the voucher's bond is slashed too. A sybil farmer can spin up identities like a comet's tail of fakes, but each one needs a real bond behind it, so the attack's cost scales linearly. Reputation then rises with a steady pulse of verified work and decays toward a nadir when an agent goes idle, so dormant fake accounts lose influence.
